provenance.canonical-source: packages/core/src/card/{Card.tsx,Card.css,CardHeader.tsx,CardHeader.css,CardContent.tsx,CardContent.css,CardFooter.tsx,CardFooter.css,hasCardSection.ts,index.ts} — the plain container — PLUS packages/core/src/interactable-card/{InteractableCard.tsx,InteractableCard.css,InteractableCardGroup.tsx,InteractableCardGroup.css,InteractableCardGroupContext.tsx,useInteractableCard.ts} and packages/core/src/link-card/{LinkCard.tsx,LinkCard.css}, which the brief puts in scope as a BEHAVIOUR AXIS (prop.interaction) rather than as separate components. All three compose the SAME CardHeader/CardContent/CardFooter parts and the same hasCardSection detector — CardContent.css, CardFooter.css and CardHeader.css each name .saltCard-sectioned, .saltLinkCard-sectioned and .saltInteractableCard-sectioned in one selector list — which is the structural argument for one canonical component. Stories read for defaults and composition: packages/core/stories/{card/card.stories.tsx,interactable-card/interactable-card.stories.tsx,link-card/link-card.stories.tsx}. Docs read for the keyboard and nesting contract: site/docs/components/card/{index,usage,accessibility}.mdx.
provenance.surface-bg-*: Card.css .saltCard-{variant} { background: var(--saltCard-background, var(--salt-container-{variant}-background)) } -> next/characteristics/container.css. primary -> palette-background-primary -> snow #FFFFFF / jet #101820; secondary -> marble #F5F7F8 / granite #1A2229; tertiary -> limestone #FAF8F2 / leather #26292B; ghost -> palette-alpha-medium, which is color-white-30a in light and color-black-30a in dark, i.e. the GHOST TONE INVERTS (next/palette/alpha.css) and is the only non-opaque tone. Values read as rgb triples from next/foundations/color.css's *-rgb entries.
provenance.surface-border: Card.css .saltCard-{variant} { border-color: var(--salt-container-{variant}-borderColor) }. All FOUR tones resolve to palette-alpha-contrast-medium -> black-30a light / white-30a dark, so the tone axis moves the background ONLY. Verified by reading all four rules, not assumed.
provenance.border-interactive: Both the hover and the active border read the SAME token family and land on the SAME value: actionable-accented-borderColor-hover and -borderColor-active are each var(--salt-palette-accent) in next/characteristics/actionable.css -> palette-accent -> blue-500 rgb(0,120,207), identical in the light and dark accent blocks, hence modeInvariant. One slot serves hover, pressed and selected.
provenance.accent-color / accent-color-focus: Card.css/InteractableCard.css `--card-accent-color: var(--salt-sentiment-accent-background)` and LinkCard.css `--linkCard-accent-color: var(--salt-sentiment-accent-background)` -> palette-accent -> blue-500. LinkCard.css's :focus-visible rule reassigns it to var(--salt-selectable-foreground-hover), which next/characteristics/selectable.css also defines as var(--salt-palette-accent) — SO THE FOCUS RECOLOUR IS A NO-OP. Both slots are carried, with identical values, so the row exists and the identity is visible rather than silently collapsed. modeInvariant because palette-accent is blue-500 in both modes.
provenance.shadow-rest / shadow-hover: Card.css/InteractableCard.css/LinkCard.css `box-shadow: var(--salt-overlayable-shadow)` and the hover/focus `var(--salt-overlayable-shadow-hover)` -> next/characteristics/overlayable.css: shadow -> palette shadow-lower, shadow-hover -> shadow-low -> next/palette/shadow.css. Matches docs/foundations/elevation.md's table exactly (lower 0 2px 4px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.1)/0.5; low 0 4px 8px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15)/0.55).
provenance.focus-outline: InteractableCard.css/LinkCard.css :focus-visible sets outline-{color,style,width,offset} individually from next/characteristics/focused.css: outlineWidth size-fixed-200 (2px, FIXED scale, density-invariant), outlineStyle borderStyle-dotted, outlineColor palette-accent-stronger -> blue-700 rgb(0,69,126) light / blue-300 rgb(154,189,245) dark, outlineOffset 0. Carried as one shorthand slot plus a separate offset in the cell, matching tabs.salt.json's treatment.
provenance.byDensity.card-padding: Card.css `--card-padding: var(--salt-spacing-200)` (declared and consumed on the same element — no lesson-2 indirection hazard) -> foundations/spacing.css spacing-200 = 2 x spacing-100 = 8/16/24/32 by density. The same value is CardHeader.css's, CardContent.css's and CardFooter.css's own padding default, so one slot serves the card and all three sections.
provenance.byDensity.card-radius: Card.css `border-radius: var(--saltCard-borderRadius, var(--salt-palette-corner, 0))` -> next/palette/corner.css [data-corner="rounded"] palette-corner -> curve-150 -> 3/6/9/12px. The ROUNDED edition pin, same as every other Salt column (docs/foundations/shape.md).
provenance.byDensity.footer-gap: CardFooter.css `gap: var(--salt-spacing-100)` -> 4/8/12/16 by density. It is the only gap in the whole Salt card.
provenance.byDensity.accent-size: Card.css .saltCard-accent{Bottom,Top,Left,Right}::after `height`/`width: var(--salt-size-bar)` -> foundations/size.css size-bar = 2/4/6/8. FROZEN-TOKEN CHECK, run in both directions (lesson 7): size-bar is on the DENSITY scale and really moves, so snapshotting the medium 4px would have been wrong at three of four densities; size-fixed-100 (the border width and the accent's -1px inset) and size-fixed-200 (its +2px overhang) are on the FIXED scale and are density-invariant BY DESIGN per docs/foundations/sizes.md, so they are carried as plain 1px/2px in the light block rather than per density.
provenance.byDensity.group-gap: InteractableCardGroup.css `gap: var(--salt-spacing-200)` -> the same 8/16/24/32 ladder as the card's own padding.
provenance.unused-disabled-tokens: TWO Salt disabled mechanisms exist and only one is live. Card.css's `.saltCard-disabled` (border-color container-primary-borderColor-disabled -> alpha-contrast-lower; color content-primary-foreground-disabled -> foreground-primary-disabled) is reached only through Card's `disabled` prop, which Card.tsx marks **Deprecated: Use the InteractableCard component instead**. InteractableCard.css's live rule is a blanket `opacity: 0.4` + `box-shadow: none` + `outline: none` + cursor-disabled. This column takes the LIVE one; the deprecated token pair is recorded here and deliberately not slotted.
provenance.accent-scope-trim: palette-accent has a data-accent axis (blue default, teal alternate). This column pins BLUE, matching button/input/select/dialog/tabs.salt.json; only calendar.salt.json models byAccent. Recorded, not modelled.
provenance.hover-media-query: Every Salt hover rule in all three card files sits inside `@media (hover: hover)`. The generator has no @media channel (docs/INPUT-MATRIX.md finding 9), so the hover rows are emitted unconditionally — a DECLARED APPROXIMATION (docs/CARD-MATRIX.md declared approximation 2), not an oversight.
provenance.no-typography: CONFIRMED ABSENCE: Card.css, CardHeader.css, CardContent.css, CardFooter.css, InteractableCard.css and LinkCard.css between them declare NO font-family, font-size, font-weight, line-height or (outside the deprecated disabled rule) colour. A Salt card inherits everything typographic from its context; its stories supply an <H3> and a <Text>, i.e. the composed `text` component. style.surface.font and style.surface.color are off for that reason, not for want of looking.

structure.media.note: no dedicated part or rule — card.stories.tsx DefaultWithImage puts a bare as a direct child of and lets the card's own overflow:hidden clip it

structure.title.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no title subcomponent is exported from card/index.ts; every story puts an <H3> inside CardHeader, so the headline is content formatting. Identical in kind to alert.salt.json's structure.title

structure.description.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — the stories use <Text color="secondary"> inside CardHeader

structure.action.note: no dedicated part; the HeaderWithAction story composes <FlexLayout justify="space-between"> + <Button appearance="transparent"><CloseIcon/></Button> inside CardHeader — the same capability with no element of its own

structure.footer.source: CardFooter.tsx + CardFooter.css — display:flex, align-items:center, gap spacing-100

structure.accent.source: Card.css .saltCard-accent::after + the four .saltCard-accent{Bottom,Top,Left,Right} rules; InteractableCard.css and LinkCard.css carry byte-equivalent copies

structure.state-layer.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — Salt distinguishes its interaction states with elevation and border colour; there is no overlay element or alpha wash anywhere in the three card CSS files

structure.card-icon.note: no card-level icon token or rule; a glyph inside a Salt card is ordinary consumer content

structure.sectioning.source: Card.tsx calls hasCardSection(children) -> hasCardSection.ts tests `child.type === CardHeader|CardContent|CardFooter` over Children.toArray, adding .saltCard-sectioned; Card.css then states the SAME rule twice, once for that class and once inside `@supports selector(:has(*))` keyed off `:has(> .saltCardHeader, > .saltCardContent, > .saltCardFooter)`

behavior.role.source: Card.tsx sets no role at all. InteractableCard.tsx: `role = interactableCardGroup ? (multiSelect ? "checkbox" : "radio") : "button"`, with `aria-checked` written only for the radio/checkbox readings. LinkCard.tsx renders a real <a href>. Three components, five roles

behavior.tab-stop.value: roving in a single-select group, all-zero in a multi-select group, zero standalone, -1 when disabled
behavior.tab-stop.source: InteractableCard.tsx's four-branch tabIndex block; useInteractableCard.ts additionally returns `tabIndex: disabled ? -1 : 0` for the standalone case. The single-select fallback is `if (!interactableCardGroup.value && isFirstChild) tabIndex = 0`

behavior.keyboard-activation.value: enter+space on button, enter only on link
behavior.keyboard-activation.source: useInteractableCard.ts handleKeyDown: `if (event.key === "Enter" || event.key === " ") { setkeyIsDown; preventDefault(); setActive(true); onClick(event) }` — activation fires on KEYDOWN. LinkCard binds no key handler: it is a native anchor, so Enter navigates and SPACE DOES NOTHING. accessibility.mdx states both halves

behavior.pointer-activation.source: useInteractableCard.ts `onClick: !disabled ? handleClick : undefined` — a disabled card has NO handler rather than a handler that returns early. InteractableCard.tsx's own handleClick additionally calls interactableCardGroup.select(event, value) and flips local selected state

behavior.active-flag.source: useInteractableCard.ts's `active` state + its setTimeout(...,0) effect, whose comments cite Enter producing both key and click events and Firefox failing to enter :active on Space. InteractableCard.tsx applies .saltInteractableCard-active only when role === "button"

behavior.disabled-handling.value: aria-disabled + tabIndex -1 + no handler + pointer-events on descendants
behavior.disabled-handling.source: useInteractableCard.ts cardProps `"aria-disabled": disabled ? true : undefined`; InteractableCard.css `.saltInteractableCard-disabled div { pointer-events: none }`; InteractableCardGroup.tsx's element query is `querySelectorAll('.saltInteractableCard:not([disabled])')`, so a disabled card is filtered out of the arrow ring

behavior.nested-interactive.value: container on Card, control-with-embedded-affordances on InteractableCard, control-only on LinkCard
behavior.nested-interactive.source: site/docs/components/card/usage.mdx: "A default card can contain any UI element, including actionable components"; "Link cards shouldn't contain actionable components (like buttons or links), as the card itself is the interactive element"; "Interactable cards ... allow the user to embed these elements within for visual affordance"

behavior.group-navigation.source: InteractableCardGroup.tsx handleKeyDown: Space always selects; and `if (!multiSelect)` ArrowDown/ArrowRight -> select(next) then elements[next].focus(), ArrowUp/ArrowLeft -> select(prev) then focus, both with wrap-around modular arithmetic. There is NO manual mode — arrowing selects. Multi-select has no arrow branch at all

behavior.selection.source: InteractableCardGroup.tsx's useControlled value + select()/isSelected(); multiSelect toggles array membership, single-select replaces and fires onChange only `if (value !== newValue)`

prop.variant.note: Salt has no elevated/filled/outlined mechanism axis. Its own multi-value prop is a container TONE ladder and is modelled as prop.container-tone — see that row's note for why the two are not merged

prop.container-tone.source: Card.tsx `variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary" | "ghost"` with `variant = "primary"` destructured as the default — DEFAULT-FIRST. ASYMMETRY RECORDED: InteractableCard.tsx and LinkCard.tsx each declare `variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary"` — ghost exists on the plain Card only

prop.accent-placement.source: Card.tsx / InteractableCard.tsx / LinkCard.tsx `accent?: "bottom" | "top" | "left" | "right"`. THE CODE SETS NO DEFAULT — the accent classes are applied only `if (accent)`. Card.css's comment `/* Styles applied to Card if accent="bottom" (default) */` and InteractableCard.tsx's JSDoc `defaults to "bottom"` both claim one; the code wins, and bottom is listed first only because it is the value the docs and every story reach for. InteractableCard additionally carries `accentPlacement`, deprecated since 1.23.0 in favour of `accent`

prop.interaction.source: three exported components, listed default-first: Card (the unqualified export the docs open with) / InteractableCard / LinkCard. Card's own `interactable` prop reaches a deprecated in-file styling branch (.saltCard-interactable) that Card.tsx marks **Deprecated: Use the InteractableCard component instead** and that has no role, no tabIndex and no key handling — it is a styling flag only, and is recorded rather than modelled as a fourth value

prop.selection-mode.source: InteractableCardGroup.tsx `multiSelect?: boolean`, undefined by default, so single-select is the source default and is listed first. It drives the group role (radiogroup vs group), the card role (radio vs checkbox), the tab-stop regime and whether arrows navigate

prop.disabled.source: InteractableCard.tsx `disabled?: boolean`, also inheritable from InteractableCardGroup's own `disabled` through context. A capability list — the skeleton reads the per-instance prop, never value[0]. Card's identically-named prop is deprecated (see the unused-disabled-tokens provenance entry)

prop.hoverable.source: Card.tsx `hoverable?: boolean` (no default, i.e. false) -> .saltCard-hoverable, which grants the hover elevation and accent border to a card that has no role, no tab stop and no handler. A capability list

state.rest.value: 1px alpha-contrast-medium border + shadow-lower + the tone background
state.rest.note: unconditional — even a static, non-hoverable Salt card is lifted

state.focus.value: 2px dotted accent-stronger outline at offset 0 + shadow-low + pointer cursor
state.focus.source: .saltInteractableCard:focus-visible / .saltLinkCard:focus-visible; the LinkCard rule also reassigns --linkCard-accent-color to a value identical to the one it replaces

state.pressed.value: accent border + shadow BACK to rest
state.pressed.source: .saltInteractableCard-selected, .saltInteractableCard:active, .saltInteractableCard-active share one block; .saltLinkCard:active is the same idea plus cursor-active

state.selected.source: the same shared declaration block — a selected Salt card and a pressed one cannot be told apart by sight

state.disabled.value: 40% opacity, no shadow, no outline, not-allowed cursor, descendants pointer-events:none
state.disabled.source: .saltInteractableCard-disabled and its four re-statements (:focus, :focus-visible, :hover, :active) so no interaction rule can win

slot.description.note: DECLARED COMPOSITION to `text` — the stories' <Text color="secondary">

slot.action.note: no dedicated part; the affordance is composed inside CardHeader

style.surface.background.note: variant="primary" (the default), read through the indirection the tone rows reassign

style.surface.color.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — Card.css declares no `color` outside the deprecated disabled rule; a Salt card inherits its text colour

style.surface.font.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — no font-family, size, weight or line-height in any of the six Salt card CSS files

style.surface.border-width.source: Card.css `border-width: var(--saltCard-borderWidth, var(--salt-size-fixed-100))` = 1px, FIXED scale, density-invariant by design

style.surface.border-color.note: identical in all four tones — verified by reading all four .saltCard-{variant} rules

style.surface.padding.source: Card.css `padding: var(--saltCard-padding, var(--card-padding))` with `--card-padding: var(--salt-spacing-200)` declared on the same element

style.surface.padding@sectioned.source: Card.css `.saltCard.saltCard-sectioned { padding: 0 }` and the `:has()` copy — the card hands its padding to its sections

style.surface.gap.note: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, with a visible consequence: Salt spaces its sections by collapsing the follower's top padding (style.content/footer.padding@adjacent), so its sections BUTT TOGETHER at zero gap where shadcn's sit 24px apart

style.surface.overflow.source: Card.css / InteractableCard.css / LinkCard.css `overflow: hidden` — it clips consumer media to the corner radius AND clips the accent bar's own -1px overhang straight back off

style.surface.transition.source: Card.css `transition: box-shadow var(--salt-duration-instant) ease-in-out`; foundations/duration.css defines duration-instant as 0ms, so the declared transition has no duration. Reproduced as source has it. (.saltCard-interactable then overrides it to `none` outright.)

style.surface.pressed.source: `.saltInteractableCard:active, .saltInteractableCard-active` — box-shadow returns to overlayable-shadow and the border goes to actionable-accented-borderColor-active (the same value as -hover)

style.surface.selected.source: `.saltInteractableCard-selected` shares the declaration block above verbatim

style.surface.focus.source: `.saltInteractableCard:focus-visible` / `.saltLinkCard:focus-visible` — the ring AND a lift to the hover shadow

style.surface.pointer-events@disabled.source: `.saltInteractableCard-disabled div { pointer-events: none }` — the descendants, not the card, so the card can still show its not-allowed cursor

style.surface.tone@ghost.source: .saltCard-ghost { background: var(--salt-container-ghost-background) } -> palette-alpha-medium: 30% WHITE light / 30% BLACK dark — the tone inverts, and it is the only translucent one. Card only; InteractableCard and LinkCard do not declare it

style.accent.box.source: Card.css `.saltCard-accent::after { background-color: var(--saltCard-accent-color, var(--card-accent-color)) }` with `--card-accent-color: var(--salt-sentiment-accent-background)`

style.accent.color@focus.note: reproduced faithfully AND flagged: selectable-foreground-hover and sentiment-accent-background both resolve to palette-accent, so this declared recolour changes nothing

style.media.box.note: no rule for card media anywhere — the clipping comes from the CARD's overflow:hidden

style.header.gap.note: CardHeader.css declares padding and flex-shrink and nothing else; the internal rhythm is a consumer StackLayout

style.content.padding@adjacent.source: CardContent.css `.saltCard-sectioned > .saltCardHeader + .saltCardContent, .saltCard-sectioned > .saltCardContent + .saltCardContent { padding-top: 0 }`, restated for LinkCard and InteractableCard and again inside `@supports selector(:has(*))`

style.content.stretch.source: CardContent.css `.saltCard-sectioned > .saltCardContent { flex: 1 1 auto }` — the EqualHeightSections story is the demonstration

style.footer.padding@adjacent.source: CardFooter.css `.saltCard-sectioned > .saltCardHeader + .saltCardFooter, .saltCard-sectioned > .saltCardContent + .saltCardFooter { padding-top: 0 }` — note the source lists header and content only, NOT footer-after-footer

style.group.box.source: InteractableCardGroup.css `gap: var(--salt-spacing-200)`; its display/flex-direction/flex-wrap are chassis layout in the template's base
